question: Why should a geological section never show a vertical fault?
answer: A fault's lean shows which block lies on top, and so whether the rock slid down (normal) or was pushed up (reverse). A vertical fault hides both, so to a geologist it reads as a sign that the setting was not understood. Leaning the fault, even a little, keeps the movement visible.
move: Always lean a fault: its tilt is the kinematics.
